title: GCP fundamentals -- Projects, Folders, Organizations, billing
exp: GCP's resource hierarchy is conceptually close to Azure's Management Group/Subscription structure, but the Project is the true fundamental unit -- almost everything in GCP lives inside exactly one Project.
pts: Organization: the root node, tied to a Google Workspace or Cloud Identity domain -- optional for a personal/small setup, standard for any real company.
Folder: an optional grouping layer between Organization and Project, used to apply policy to a department or environment (e.g. a 'Production' folder containing several related projects).

Project: the fundamental unit almost everything lives inside -- billing, quotas, and IAM policy are all scoped primarily at the Project level. This is the closest single analog to an AWS Account, closer than a Subscription is on Azure.

Every resource has a globally unique Project ID (not just a display name) baked into its identifiers -- somewhat like how an S3 bucket name must be globally unique, but applied at the Project level instead of per-resource.

Billing Account is a separate top-level construct linked to one or more Projects -- a single Billing Account can fund many Projects, and a Project can be moved between Billing Accounts, a genuinely different model from how AWS ties billing directly to the Account itself.
Set a budget alert on the Billing Account immediately -- the GCP equivalent of the AWS/Azure billing-alarm habit, and arguably the most important five minutes of setup on any new GCP environment.
code:
# gcloud CLI -- fundamentals
gcloud auth login
gcloud projects list

gcloud projects create orders-pipeline-prod --name="Orders Pipeline"
gcloud config set project orders-pipeline-prod

# Link a Billing Account to the project
gcloud billing projects link orders-pipeline-prod \
  --billing-account=XXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXX

# Budget alert -- set this immediately on any new project
gcloud billing budgets create \
  --billing-account=XXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXX \
  --display-name="SpendingAlert-20USD" \
  --budget-amount=20USD \
  --threshold-rule=percent=1.0
pr: Create a GCP Project, link it to a Billing Account, and set a budget alert at $20

r: No direct AWS equivalent -- funds multiple Projects

qa.q: What is the fundamental unit of organization in GCP, and how does it compare to an AWS Account or an Azure Subscription?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** The Project. Nearly every resource, IAM policy, and quota is scoped primarily at the Project level -- it's the closest single analog to an AWS Account, arguably closer than an Azure Subscription is, since Azure additionally has Resource Groups as a meaningful sub-Subscription organizational layer that GCP's Project doesn't have an equivalent of within itself.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Instantiating new HttpClient() instances manually causes socket exhaustion in OS TIME_WAIT state under high concurrency. Fix: register typed clients with IHttpClientFactory to manage handler lifetimes and DNS refresh.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** IHttpClientFactory prevents socket leaks and manages DNS rotation, but requires explicit Polly retry and circuit breaker policies to prevent cascade failures during downstream outages.

qa.q: How does GCP's Billing Account relationship to Projects differ structurally from how AWS ties billing to an Account?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** A Billing Account is a separate, standalone construct that can fund multiple Projects simultaneously, and a Project can be relinked to a different Billing Account over its lifetime. AWS ties billing directly to the Account itself -- there's no equivalent of a separate billing entity funding multiple otherwise-independent Accounts in the same lightweight way. This makes GCP's model slightly more flexible for scenarios like a single company Billing Account funding many independent team Projects.
